tree: Catches the sum that doesn’t add up.

Each line is worked out from its quantity and price, then added up and compared with the total printed on the invoice. If they differ, or a line can’t be read, the scan is flagged before it reaches your books.

tree: What does it read from an invoice?
The supplier, the date, each line with quantity and price, and the printed total.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: What if the total doesn’t match the lines?
The scan is flagged with the difference and any line it couldn’t read, so you can check before approving.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: Where do scanned receipts end up?
As expenses by default. You can send any row somewhere else, such as a supplier record, during review.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: Can I keep the paper copy digitally?
Yes. The original photo or PDF stays attached to the scan.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: No. The expense is prepared for you and saved only after you approve it.
